title: Canada's Express Entry Pool Shrinks to 231,533 as Competition Intensifies
excerpt: IRCC's latest pool data shows a 3,594-candidate decline from the previous update, with top-scoring profiles continuing to thin out after 35 draws and nearly 90,000 invitations issued in 2026.
body:
• Canada's Express Entry pool has decreased to 231,533 active profiles as of July 19, 2026.
  • In 2026, 89,601 invitations to apply have been issued, mainly for Canadian Experience Class candidates.
  • The 501–600 CRS score range has grown to 18,133 profiles, indicating increased competition among high-scoring candidates.
  • The latest CEC draw had a cut-off score of 516, while the PNP draw cut-off was significantly higher at 744.

IRCC Data

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has published updated data on the composition of the Express Entry candidate pool, revealing a system under sustained pressure from high application volumes and an increasingly competitive top tier.

https://x.com/TundeTASH/status/2079587520866644463

As of July 19, 2026, the pool held 231,533 active profiles — a net decrease of 3,594 from the 235,127 recorded on July 5. That earlier count itself marked a drop of 4,518 from the June 21 snapshot of 239,645, driven by four draws that issued a combined 9,226 invitations between the two dates.

Where the Candidates Are

The distribution tells a story of growing strength at the top and persistent congestion in the middle. The 501–600 CRS score band now holds 18,133 profiles, down slightly from the July 5 count but substantially higher than the 13,000 average at the beginning of 2026. According to Moving2Canada, this growth indicates that more high-scoring candidates are entering the pool faster than IRCC is issuing invitations — a pattern that could keep Canadian Experience Class (CEC) cut-off scores elevated.

The largest concentration remains in the 451–500 range, with 72,579 candidates — a decrease of 1,112 from the previous update. The 401–450 band holds 63,877, while the 351–400 range has stayed relatively stable at 51,107. Below 300, just 7,836 candidates remain, with virtually no realistic path to invitation outside the Physicians with Canadian Work Experience category.

Draw Patterns in 2026

Through 35 draws conducted by late July, IRCC has issued 89,601 ITAs. The distribution across draw types reveals a clear strategic focus:

Canadian Experience Class draws dominate, accounting for 45,250 ITAs across 12 rounds, with recent cut-off scores hovering between 514 and 518. French-language proficiency draws follow with 35,500 ITAs across seven rounds, reflecting Canada's bilingualism priorities. Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) draws have issued 6,450 ITAs across 14 rounds, while sector-specific draws for healthcare, trades, physicians, and senior managers make up the remainder.

The July 20 PNP draw set a cut-off of 744 for 511 invitations — the lowest PNP threshold since November 2025, according to CIC News. A day later, a CEC draw issued 2,000 invitations at a cut-off of 516.

Indians constitute the largest nationality group in the Express Entry system. For candidates scoring in the 451–500 range, competition remains fierce but the path is active: CEC, French-language, and trades draws regularly pull from this tier. Those in the 401–450 range face longer odds, with movement primarily driven by French-language draws that require strong bilingual test scores.

Candidates scoring below 400 should focus on concrete score-improvement strategies: a provincial nomination adds 600 points, Canadian work experience can add 40–80 points depending on duration, and improved language test scores — particularly in French — can yield substantial gains. IRCC's 2026 draw pattern makes clear that in-Canada experience and French proficiency are the two fastest routes to an invitation.

"The pool not only refills quickly but also with higher numbers than at the beginning of 2026, when the average number of active profiles in the 601–1200 range was 345 between February and May."

— Moving2Canada analysis

Looking Ahead

2026 Draw Insights
›45,250 ITAs from Canadian Experience Class draws.
›35,500 ITAs from French-language proficiency draws.
›6,450 ITAs from Provincial Nominee Program draws.
›Lowest PNP cut-off since November 2025 was 744.

With the pool shrinking modestly but high-scoring segments growing, the overall trajectory points to sustained or increasing competition. IRCC has yet to conduct a general all-program draw in 2026, maintaining its strategy of category-specific selections. For candidates without Canadian experience or French skills, the gap between their scores and the invitation threshold continues to widen.

The next pool distribution update is expected in early August. In the meantime, candidates can check their competitiveness against current pool data: a score of 501 or higher places a candidate in the top 8.14% of the pool, while a score of 451 puts them in the top 32.94%.
